units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:5">Ab. III, 5</cite> <he>עול מ׳</he> the yoke of (secular) government (burden of office).
<cite ref="Berakhot 13b:18">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>עול מ׳ שמים</he> the yoke of (submission to) divine government.
<cite ref="Berakhot 48b:9">Ber. 48ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>אין מ׳ נוגעת וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00109"><he>חָבֵר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sotah 11b:22">Sot. 11ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>בתים</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 1:21">Ex. I, 21</cite>) <he>בתי מ׳</he> dynasties.—<he>מרד במ׳</he> to rebel against the government, to commit treason.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 49a">Snh. 49ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>מ׳ הָרִשְׁעָה</he> the wicked government (Rome).
<cite ref="Berakhot 61b:9">Ber. 61ᵇ</cite> Ms. M. a. early ed. (later ed. <he>יון</he>); a. fr.—<he>קרוב למ׳</he> connected with the court (influential).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 44:17">Gen. R. s. 44</cite> <he>ארבעה … גיהינם ומ׳ וכ׳</he> the Lord showed him (Abraham) four things: future punishment, (persecution by foreign) governments &c.; Mekh. Yithro, s. 9 <he>ארבע מ׳ וכ׳</he> the four empires which were destined to subject his descendants.

<cite ref="Berakhot 34b:20">Ber. 34ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>אין בין … אלא שעבוד מ׳ מלבד</he> there will be no difference (in the conditions of life) between the present and the Messianic days except (the delivery from) the oppression of governments; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (in liturgy) a benediction invoking God as king (אלהינו מלך העולם). Ib. 12ᵃ כל ברכה שאין בה מ׳ וכ׳ a benediction in which the word ‘king’ does not occur, is no benediction.—Pl. מַלְכִיּוֹת the references to the divine kingdom in the Musaf of the New Year’s Day, the section called Malkhiyoth.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:6">Ib. 6</cite> <he>עשרה מ׳</he> the recitation of ten Biblical verses referring to the divine government.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:6">Ib.</cite> (32ᵇ) <he>זכרונות מ׳ וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. sing.), v. <cite ref="G00470"><he>זִכָּרוֹן</he></cite>. Y. ib. III, 58ᵈ; a. e.
